candidates.name: Illugastaðir seal hide (Vatnsnes)
candidates.zh: 伊魯加斯塔濟海豹觀察點

may.note: Closed for eider nesting: the Seal Center's notice says 6 May to 20 June (a 2024 post); Visit Iceland says May and June; another listing says until 29 June. 5/2 is before the 6 May date, so it should be open on the trip date but the 2027 date is not fixed. About 800-900 m walk to a hide; bring binoculars; seal numbers depend on tide.

Open year-round trail, but sources put best seal chances in June to August at low tide; Nordic Visitor says June or July. Early May seal numbers are not documented. Wikidata Q137838904 has no label, so no Q-id is given.
Viewpoint with fulmars and puffins nesting; no seasonal limits given. Puffins return around May, so early May may be before peak.
Exterior and lava-field setting are always accessible; interior opening not documented. Wikidata label is 'Búðir Church'.
Year-round; parking is paid per a 2026 note (1,400 ISK per car, 24 h, private land). Kirkjufellsfoss is Q2447177.
Town is open; hours of the Volcano Museum and Library of Water on Sunday 5/2 were not checked.
Crater trail near Bifröst; no seasonal info in sources read.
Remains accessible during the Illugastaðir eider closure (Seal Center). Visit at low tide to see it close; seal colony nearby. Lack of marked paths has trampled nesting areas, so stay on routes.
Volcanic plug with fort ruins; the access road can be wet or snowy in spring, not verified.
Canyon viewpoint; no seasonal info in sources read.
Guided tours only; 2027 tour times not checked. Described as Iceland's longest lava tube.

Fodor's listing (seen only as a search snippet; Fodor's page returned 403) says closed Sept to May. Not verified against a primary source; the exterior by Hóp lagoon is visible regardless.

Accessible on foot; marked trails over lava with hidden crevices. Parking reported 1,000 ISK, free with a purchase at the cafe (search snippet). Snow or mud on trails in early May and cafe hours not documented.
Short loop trail. Mývatn Visitor Centre at Skútustaðir daily 09:00-18:00 per Wikivoyage (undated). Mývatn waterfowl visible from the shore.
Open in all seasons (Guide to Iceland); Wikivoyage lists winter hours 12:00-22:00 and summer 09:00-00:00, undated. Exact 3-5 May hours not found.

Access road from Route 1 near Vogar is poor but passable for cars in summer and often impassable in winter; if blocked, parking at the Ring Road adds about 3 km of walking (search snippet). Rim climb about 600 m, 10-25 min; rim loop 3.2 km, about 1 h. Snow and ice possible, traction devices advised by some guides; ust.is lists no spring-thaw closure. Crater floor is off limits.

Route 863 snow state in early May is not stated by any source read, and no 2027 or recent road notice was found. Guide to Iceland calls May a shoulder season with most Krafla attractions accessible, and flags winter snow and ice on geothermal trails; Visit Akureyri says mountain roads open gradually through June. Check road.is before Day 4/5. Swimming not allowed.
Same road 863 as Víti; no early-May road or path state found. Boardwalk paths must be followed; avoid in poor visibility (Guide to Iceland).
Walking paths and birch trees; no seasonal restriction or closure found. Coordinates from the Visit North Iceland page (DMS converted); Q1067075 is the Reykjavík Höfði and is not this place.
Lava pillars and rock outcrops in and around the bay next to Höfði; no seasonal or access information found. Coordinates are the OSM way for Kálfaströnd; the bay name has no Wikidata entry.
Private land, guided tour only with ice sculptures inside; no 3-5 May tour schedule found.

may.note: Official site: 1 Nov to 14 May daily 14:00-16:00; 15 to 31 May daily 14:00-16:00; June to Aug 12:00-17:00. Mon 3 and Tue 4 May fall 14:00-16:00. Adults 2,400 ISK. Closed from 1 Nov 2026 until after New Year (phone 846 7245). Wikivoyage's 11:00-19:00 is outdated.

Wikipedia: most ducks migrate in from north-western Europe in late April to early May, so arrival is under way but not complete on 4 May; Barrow's goldeneye are resident (about 2,000). Fun Iceland says spring and early summer are richest; no ice-off date found. Neslönd bird-nesting area is closed to access in nesting season (Wikivoyage).

About 250 pairs on the Laxá outflow (Wikipedia). No source gives a harlequin arrival date; migrants generally arrive late April to early May. Coordinates are the lake centre; the Wikidata point for Laxá is its mouth about 40 km away.

Coordinates approximate (farm is about 400 m west of Sel-Hotel Mývatn, Skútustaðir).

decision.why: 從 Akureyri 來回約 80 km，會壓縮 Dettifoss 的時間

may.note: Guide to Iceland names Vatnsnes (Route 711, gravel, 2-3 h loop; Illugastaðir hide; Ósar below Hvítserkur Q201855) as the reliable site; peak is July and pups are born late May to early June; Illugastaðir closes during eider nesting. In Eyjafjörður, ringed seals appear April to June but are rare and solitary, with no viewing site. Not on the Day 3-5 route.

Whale Museum (Q2543158): May hours 09:00-18:00 daily in most listings, one says 08:30-18:30 (search snippets). Exploration Museum: 15 May to 31 Aug daily 11-17, 1 Sep to 14 May Tue-Fri 13-16 and Sat 11-16, so Mon 3 May is closed. Church Q16429000 hours not found. Whale-watching tours excluded separately.

Gljúfrastofa visitor centre: 1 to 31 May daily 10:00-17:00 (Jan 2 to Apr 30 weekdays 11-15). Road 862 is paved with winter service from mid-March and joins Route 85 at Ásbyrgi; Route 85 and the final stretch can ice or close after snow (search snippet). No live 2027 road state; check road.is. Campsite from 15 May (not needed).

Road 842 has no winter service, and the last 4 km (F26 track) is 4x4-only and closes with snow; secondary roads 842 and 843 are generally closed in winter (search snippets). No early-May opening found; Fun Iceland says it needs more planning. Treat as unreachable until a Vegagerðin notice says otherwise.

decision.why: 842 號沒有冬季服務，最後 4 km 限四驅

may.note: Highland destination sold as a summer day tour (Guide to Iceland zh); F-roads normally open from June at the earliest and Visit Akureyri reported mountain roads opening gradually in June 2026. No specific F88 notice read, so closure on 3-5 May is inferred.

decision.why: 高地 F 路，通常 6 月才開

may.note: Tours run year-round from Akureyri harbour, Hauganes and Húsavík per Guide to Iceland and Visit Akureyri; excluded from the plan. Wikidata point is the fjord Eyjafjörður.

Excluded: needs a flight or ferry from Dalvík (ferry Mon and Wed per winter listing). Puffins are on the island from late April to early August (Visit North Iceland). Q213707 is the settlement; Q2347299 is a different Grímsey.
Excluded as a bathing site. Winter 2025-26 listing: open daily 12:00-22:00 but closed Jan to mid-March for construction; Guide to Iceland says open year-round.
Excluded as a bathing site. Hours not read.
Excluded as a bathing site. Wikivoyage: 2 pools, hot tubs, slides, 450 kr (old); Sep to May winter hours Mon-Fri 06:45-21:00 (undated).

fjalladyrd.is lists cafes Beitarhúsið 08:30-20:00 and Fjallakaffi 07:30-22:00 with no season dates; one Guide to Iceland snippet calls the farm open year-round. Early-May hours not confirmed; call +354 894 8181.

east.is: road 923 is gravel, accessible to all cars and open all year; spring thaw turns the river grey-brown (blue colour is not reliable in May); pink-footed geese nest in the area 1 May-10 June so stay on marked trails. West-side Grund platforms are the easy option; east-side Klaustursel hike is harder in snow/ice. Vegagerðin paved/rebuilt a 4.6 km section of road 923 in 2025 (completion not confirmed).

candidates.name: Hafnarhólmi puffin colony
candidates.zh: 哈夫納霍爾米海鸚棲地

may.note: east.is: puffins nest mid-April to early August; first sightings reported 12 Apr 2023 and 8 Apr 2025 (east.is spring blog), so birds should be present on 5/6; east.is also lists common eiders, kittiwakes and fulmars nesting there. No opening hours or May-specific access rules are published; Ascension Day impact unknown. Road 94 is paved all the way (visiticeland/earthtrekkers via snippet).

Town and Route 93 over Fjarðarheiði are normally passable in May but the pass can close at short notice in winter-type weather (April 2017 stranding). Ascension Day 5/6 shop and museum hours unknown; check road.is that morning.

Trail 40-60 min uphill each way (east.is). May sources disagree: Komoot says typically snow/ice free in spring, Travel Dojo says muddy or icy early in the season; carry ice spikes. No fee or closure published.

Grapevine (June 2025, via search snippet) gives 1 May-15 Oct, daily 09:00-17:00, ISK 2,000; Guide to Iceland gives a narrower Jun-Sep, Sunday closed, which looks stale. 5/7 is a Friday. Official site steinapetra.is not read.
Harbour, Eggin í Gleðivík and the shore walk are outdoors and always reachable. Papey boat trips run June-August only.

candidates.name: Eggin í Gleðivík (Eggs of Merry Bay)

may.note: Visit Iceland (search result): open every day, 10:00-17:00 from 19 Aug to 31 May; seals are among the animals. Other listings differ slightly; no May seal-feeding time found (a one-off 11:00 seal feeding appeared in a February event).
